question: The outer Himalayas is also known as _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiwaliks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The Shiwaliks are also known as Outer Himalayas.
 
• They are located in between the Great Northern Plains and the Lesser Himalayas.
 
• The Himalayan Frontal Fault separates the Northern Plains of India from the Shiwalik range.
 
• The altitude of Shiwaliks varies from 600 to 1500 metres.
 
• They run for a distance of 2,400 km from the Potwar Plateau to the Brahmaputra valley.
 
• 
 
The width of the Shiwaliks varies from 50 km in Himachal Pradesh to less than 15 km in Arunachal Pradesh.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A fault is a crack in the Earth's lithosphere that occurs between two pieces of rock. 
 
• Faults can range in length from a few millimeters to thousands of kilometers and are found all over the world. 
 
• The term fault came from the Old French term *falte*, which means opening or gap.
 
• 
 There are three different types of faults, which are separated by how the sections of rock move in relation to each other along the fault:

 
 
• Dip-Slip Faults __- occur at an angle in comparison to the surface of Earth
 
• __Strike-Slip Faults__ - rocks slide past one another
 
• __Oblique-Slip Faults__ - combine dip-slip and strike-slip movements
